text:
Aisha Bello: heads up: once the saturation signals land in prod next week, we need to tune alerts + paging so we don’t melt the on-call with noise. can we align on thresholds + what actually pages vs just posts to #eng-sre-alerts?

Aisha Bello: proposal (v0) based on the standard + what we saw in the metrics audit:
- WARNING (Slack only):
  - gpu_queue_depth_p95 > 10 for 10m
  - throttled_requests_rate > 1% for 10m
  - kv_cache_pressure > 0.80 for 15m
  - scheduler_contention > 0.50 for 10m
- PAGE (PD): only if saturation *and* user symptom in same 10m window:
  - (gpu_queue_depth_p95 > 20 for 5m OR throttled_requests_rate > 2% for 5m) AND (p95_latency_slo_breach OR 5xx_rate > 0.5%)

Aisha Bello: also: keep per-model/per-route labels out of paging alerts (too much cardinality). page at service+region+cluster.

Sean Gallagher: +1 on “saturation alone doesn’t page”. we’ve been burned by GPU util pages that weren’t customer-impacting.

Sean Gallagher: can we sanity check the queue depth numbers? 10/20 feels aggressive if we’re doing continuous batching.

Allison Grant: pulling from the saturation standard doc (the one we published last week): queue depth is the most actionable, but it’s super dependent on scheduler config.

Allison Grant: I’m more confident on throttling + scheduler contention thresholds than raw GPU util. GPU util tends to sit high even when happy.

Allison Grant: recommended defaults from the doc were:
- queue_depth: warn > 10 (10m), critical > 25 (5m)
- throttling: warn > 1%, critical > 3% (5m)
- kv cache: warn > 0.80 (15m), critical > 0.90 (10m)

Logan Wright: telemetry POV: gpu_queue_depth_p95 is stable across regions now after label normalization, but it *does* spike during deploys / warmup.

Logan Wright: would strongly suggest adding a “recent deploy in region within last 15m” mute/annotation rather than bumping threshold. otherwise we just desensitize.

Rafael Mendes: agree w/ Logan. paging policy should also respect incident-bot context: if deploy collector shows canary rollout, responders can make a faster call.

Rafael Mendes: question: do we want a separate page for “metrics backend lag / missing data”? we saw that during the last game-day.

Caleb Johnson: for missing data, I’d rather do Slack-only “signal degraded” + dashboard link.

Caleb Johnson: if we page on telemetry lag we’ll page ourselves during any ingest blip. we can add a heartbeat alert to observability rotation instead.

Miles Thornton: multi-region note: we should avoid paging globally if only one region is saturated.

Miles Thornton: can we set alert labels to region + capacity tier (hosted vs dedicated)? dedicated customers escalate faster, hosted can degrade gracefully.

Aisha Bello: yep, was planning to split rules by tier. for hosted we can gate paging on actual SLO breach. for dedicated we probably page on sustained throttling even if latency hasn’t breached yet (since they have hard throughput expectations).

Jacob Stein: from incident-bot side: if we keep the thresholds stable, I can have the saturation collector highlight “above warn/above critical” with the same semantics as alerting. avoids confusion.

Sean Gallagher: makes sense. I want one shared vocabulary:
- “elevated” = warn threshold
- “critical” = page threshold

Sean Gallagher: on queue depth: I’d prefer critical at 25 vs 20 (less pager noise). queue depth is also bursty on large prompts.

Allison Grant: +1. also: can we swap scheduler_contention > 0.50 to > 0.60 for page? 0.50 is often just “busy but fine” during peak.

Aisha Bello: updated v1:
- WARNING (Slack only):
  - gpu_queue_depth_p95 > 10 for 10m
  - throttled_requests_rate > 1% for 10m
  - kv_cache_pressure > 0.80 for 15m
  - scheduler_contention > 0.50 for 10m
- PAGE (PD), hosted tier:
  - (gpu_queue_depth_p95 > 25 for 5m OR throttled_requests_rate > 3% for 5m OR kv_cache_pressure > 0.90 for 10m) AND (p95_latency_slo_breach OR 5xx_rate > 0.5%)
- PAGE (PD), dedicated tier:
  - throttled_requests_rate > 3% for 5m OR gpu_queue_depth_p95 > 25 for 10m (no SLO gate)

Aisha Bello: and add a 15m “deploy in region” annotation + optional mute for WARNING only (not for PAGE).

Logan Wright: love that. if you want, I can wire the deploy annotation into the alert template so it shows “last deploy: <sha> <time>” when it fires. saves a click.

Rafael Mendes: re paging policy update: I’ll update the PD service:
- remove the old “GPU util > 95%” page entirely
- route new saturation pages to primary on-call (SRE)
- warnings to #eng-sre-alerts + tag @oncall-sre (no page)

Rafael Mendes: also add note in the on-call runbook: “do not mitigate based on saturation alone; confirm with latency/errors + deploy/config context.”

Sean Gallagher: :thumbsup: please add a short section on “when to invoke graceful degradation” (reduce max tokens, lower concurrency caps, route to smaller model) once saturation critical hits.

Jacob Stein: I can add a bot snippet that posts suggested levers when it detects critical saturation (just text + links, no auto-mitigation). will match this policy.

Allison Grant: can you all ensure the dashboard links in the alert go to the canonical saturation dashboard (not the old per-cluster one)? we’ve got the new one in observability-pack PR 0321.

Aisha Bello: yep. I’ll:
1) lock these thresholds in the rules PR
2) update paging policy + runbook text
3) post rollout plan in #eng-sre + ask rotations to opt-in for week 1

Miles Thornton: last ask: can we set “for:” durations slightly longer in EU? we’ve got noisier sampling there during off-peak.

Caleb Johnson: we can do per-region “for” overrides, but I’d rather keep uniform unless we have evidence. can we try uniform for 1 week + revisit with alert volume metrics?

Aisha Bello: agree. we’ll run uniform for week 1, track:
- pages/day caused by saturation rules
- % with confirmed customer impact
- time-to-suspect-change (from bot)

Sean Gallagher: sounds good. thanks all. please post the final thresholds + PD changes in this thread before merging so we have a record.

Aisha Bello: will do. (and if anyone sees pager noise first week, drop a note + link the alert firing instance so we can tune fast.)
